analysis.title: US Weekly Kickstart: Q3 2026 earnings season preview
key_insights: Q3 2026 earnings season starts the week of October 12 with 7% of S&P 500 market cap reporting. About 70% will have reported by the end of October. Most hyperscalers report the last week of October and Nvidia reports around November 19.

Consensus expects S&P 500 EPS growth of 27% y/y in Q3, the highest heading into any reporting season since 2021. That compares with realized growth of 33% in Q2, excluding 'other income' from equity stakes. GS expects most companies to beat consensus again.
Options imply an average earnings-day move of 5.4% for the average S&P 500 stock this quarter, versus 5.5% implied over the past 4 quarters and a 5.1% average realized move.

Info Tech and Energy are expected to contribute nearly 80% of Q3 S&P 500 EPS growth. The median stock in each is expected to grow EPS by more than 30% y/y. Consumer sectors show no aggregate EPS growth in bottom-up estimates.

AI infrastructure stocks are expected to drive more than half of Q3 S&P 500 EPS growth. The top 10 contributors account for over two-thirds of growth, and Micron and Nvidia together account for more than one third.
Micron reported this week with y/y EPS growth of 1,003%, beat consensus EPS and gave strong forward guidance.
Market breadth is the narrowest since the Dot Com Bubble. The index is 2% from its all-time high while the median stock is 17% below its high. Both earnings and returns are concentrated in Info Tech.

For the median S&P 500 stock, consensus EPS growth slows from 14% in Q2 to 9% in Q3. Median sales growth slows from 7% to 6%. Consensus expects deceleration in every sector except Info Tech and Comm Services.

Margin pressure: consensus has the median stock's net margin at 14.7% in Q3 versus 15.1% in Q2. Analysts cut Q3 median margin estimates by 11 bp since the start of the quarter, in every sector except Info Tech. Input costs limit sequential margin expansion.
The weaker dollar boosted S&P 500 revenue growth by roughly 2 pp in Q1 and 1 pp in Q2, and GS estimates less than 1 pp in Q3. GS economists estimate nominal GDP grew 6% y/y in Q3, similar to Q2.

Consensus has hyperscaler capex growing 116% y/y in Q3 versus 87% in Q2. GS expects 2027 hyperscaler capex growth above 50%, above the roughly $1.1 trillion consensus, though the pace of capex growth and upside surprises should diminish. GS does not expect clarity on 2028 capex this season.
Hyperscaler cloud revenue growth accelerated to 48% in Q2. GS equity analysts expect 55% in Q3. Cloud revenue backlogs are large and growing, which GS reads as monetization of AI capex.
About 50% of S&P 500 firms discussed AI productivity or efficiency on last quarter's calls, but only 2% quantified the earnings impact. GS expects these shares to rise gradually.
Mega-cap tech booked about $150 billion of accounting profit from appreciating equity stakes last quarter, 12% of S&P 500 EPS. GS expects this 'other income' distortion to fade in Q3.

Tariff refunds were $77 billion in Q2 and $69 billion in Q3, roughly 6% of US corporate pre-tax profits each quarter. Most firms in an Atlanta Fed survey plan to keep the refunds in cash or invest in R&D or capital projects.
GS top-down S&P 500 forecasts: YE 2026 target 8000 (about 4% above the current 7666) and 12-month target 8700. 2026 EPS $375, 2027 EPS $415 versus bottom-up consensus $365 and $421.
The GS US Equity Sentiment Indicator is at -0.7, which is between light and neutral positioning. The S&P 500 trades at 19x NTM EPS versus 15x for the equal-weight index.

earnings_insights: S&P 500 Q3 2026 consensus EPS growth is 27% y/y (consensus est), the highest heading into a season since 2021, versus 33% realized in Q2 excluding 'other income'.
Median S&P 500 stock consensus EPS growth is 9% y/y in Q3 (consensus est) versus 14% in Q2. Ex-Financials and Utilities, consensus S&P 500 EPS growth is 36%.

Consensus Q3 sector EPS growth: Energy 109%, Info Tech 64%, Comm Services 38%, Materials 36%, Industrials 16%, Real Estate 15%, Utilities 6%, Health Care 5%, Financials 1%, Consumer Discretionary 0%, Consumer Staples -0%.
Micron reported fiscal Q results on September 30 (printed) with y/y EPS growth of 1,003%, beating consensus EPS estimates with strong forward guidance.
Expected report dates: GOOGL and BA October 27, META October 29, XOM, AMZN and CVX October 30, MPC November 3, NVDA November 19, AVGO December 11.
Consensus expects S&P 500 revenue/sales growth of 9% in Q3 (12% ex-Financials and Utilities), with ex-Financials and Utilities net margin of 15%, up 252 bp.
GS top-down 2026 S&P 500 EPS is $375 (+36% y/y) versus bottom-up consensus $365 (+33%) and top-down strategist consensus $355 (+29%). 2027 EPS is $415 (GS), $421 (bottom-up) and $410 (strategists).

risk_factors: Narrow breadth and concentration: the top 10 contributors drive over two-thirds of Q3 EPS growth.
Input cost pressures are trimming margin estimates in every sector except Info Tech.
A smaller dollar tailwind to revenue growth in Q3.
Uncertainty over 2028 AI capex, which GS does not expect companies to clarify this season.
Slowing upside surprises and capex growth relative to recent quarters.
Consumer sectors show no aggregate EPS growth.

tension_points.bull_case: Consensus Q3 EPS growth of 27% is the highest entering a season since 2021, macro data is strong, revision breadth is positive and GS expects most companies to beat.
tension_points.bear_case: Growth is concentrated: AI infrastructure drives over half of EPS growth, the median stock's growth slows to 9% from 14%, margins are being cut and breadth is the weakest since the Dot Com Bubble.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Hyperscalers or AI infrastructure names missing or cutting capex and cloud growth guidance in the last week of October.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscaler capex is expected to grow 116% in Q3 and more than 50% in 2027, above the roughly $1.1 trillion consensus, with cloud revenue accelerating to 55%.
tension_points.bear_case: GS expects the pace of capex growth and upside surprises to diminish, and investor focus is on uncertainty around 2028 spending that companies are not expected to address.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Cloud revenue growth failing to accelerate from 48% in Q3 reports, which would weaken the monetization case.
